newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Epic wins Kingstream gas transport contract.
newsitem.headline: Epic wins Kingstream gas transport contract.

text.p: Kingstream Resources NL and Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd awarded a 15-year gas transportation contract to Epic Energy Pty Ltd to transport up to 170 terajoules of gas a day to its proposed A$1.5 billion steel project in Western Australia starting in 2000, Kingstream said on Wednesday.
Kingstream also said it expects to shore up gas supply contracts for the plant shortly.

"We will soon be awarding the equally important contract for supply of gas as well as that for builder/operator of the power station and also the preferred ore to steel process technology," Kingstream chairman Ken Court said in a statement.
Kingstream shareholders are scheduled to meet on June 18 to consider a merger proposal with An Feng.

A likely source of the gas fro the project would be from the huge reserves of the offshore North West Shelf, although several gas producers operating offshore in central and northern Western Australia have expressed interest, an Epic spokeswoman said.
The transport contract was worth between A$350 million and A$450 million, she said.
In total, gas supply and transport costs represent about 30 percent of the A$1.5 billion project's input costs, Court said.
Under the agreement reached on Wednesday, Epic will spend A$300 million to expand the 1,500 km Dampier-Bunbury natural gas pipeline in order to transport the gas.
Epic will ship the gas via a 55 km lateral pipeline from the Dampier pipeline to the steel plant, to be located north of Geraldton.

The agreement also provides for the volume of gas to increase significantly over the life of the contract in line with expected increases in Kingstream's steel production from an initial 2.4 million tonnes a year to up to about five million tonnes, Court said.

The gas is needed for the steel plant's direct reduction iron processing component and also for a gas-fired power station, which will power the electric arc furnaces during the steel manufacturing process.
Allgas Energy Ltd, the AMP Investments arm of The Australian Mutual Provident Society, AXIOM Funds Management and Hastings Funds Management each holds 10 percent interests in Epic.
The remaining 60 percent is held 30-30 by El Paso Energy Corp and Consolidated Natural Gas Co's CNG International unit.
